justin.name: Justin

hard_no: onions (all types: white, red, yellow, green, shallots, scallions, leeks)
restrictions.notes: Garlic is OK. No other restrictions.

justin.notes: Generally flexible eater aside from the onion restriction.

jaclyn.name: Jaclyn
jaclyn.notes: Would be happy with roasted sweet potatoes every week.

cora.name: Cora
cora.notes: Adventurous with Asian flavors and seafood.

eve.name: Eve
eve.notes: Prefers red meat and fried foods. Not big on fish or chicken. Does NOT like cooked bell peppers.

household_rules.meal_structure: 3 entrees + 3-4 shared sides per week (at least 1 salad when attendance calls for salad); no weekly sweet/treat unless explicitly requested
household_rules.portion_sizing: Each entree should yield 4-6 servings depending on who's home that week (see attendance_scaling). Let recipes dictate natural protein quantities — do NOT override with fixed minimums. Target enough for the planned number of diners with comfortable seconds, not excessive leftovers.

everyone_home.label: Full house (Justin + Jaclyn + Cora + Eve)
everyone_home.salad: big batch (Justin eats most of it — size to last several days)

justin_traveling.label: Justin away (Jaclyn + Cora + Eve)
justin_traveling.salad: skip — nobody eats enough to justify it

jaclyn_traveling.label: Jaclyn away (Justin + Cora + Eve)
jaclyn_traveling.sweet_potatoes: light or skip — she's the main consumer

household_rules.planning_day: Saturday — plan for the upcoming Mon-Sun week
household_rules.overlap_constraint: Every person must find at least 1 of the 2 weekly meals appealing
household_rules.complexity: Most meals should be executable by a 12-14 year old; occasional 90-min Sunday cook is OK
household_rules.pantry_handling: Tag pantry staples in ingredient list (olive oil, butter, salt, pepper, common spices, rice, pasta, flour, sugar, etc.) but still include them
household_rules.cheese_preference: Always prefer block cheese over pre-shredded. Shred at home — better melting, no anti-caking agents. NEVER use American cheese singles. If a slice form factor is needed (e.g. burgers), use sliced cheddar. Otherwise use block cheddar.
household_rules.produce_preference: Always prefer whole/fresh fruits and vegetables over canned or jarred alternatives. When searching Kroger, filter for fresh produce — skip canned sweet potatoes, jarred jalapeños, canned tomatoes (unless the recipe specifically calls for canned, e.g. chipotle in adobo).
household_rules.garnish_policy: Skip decorative garnishes like parsley, cilantro sprigs, etc. Only include an ingredient if it meaningfully contributes to flavor.

sides_rules.salad_sizing: Big batch if Justin is primary eater (lasts days); small if mostly Jaclyn+girls (finish in 2 days). Default: size up for Justin.
sides_rules.salad_variety: Rotate lettuce types (romaine, mixed greens, arugula, butter lettuce, spinach, etc.) and maximize topping variety (must be Kroger-deliverable).
sides_rules.remaining_sides: Healthy, high-fiber, whole-food. No highly processed. Color variety across vegetables.
sides_rules.starch_limit: At most 1 starchy side per week, modest portions. Sweet potato preferred over white potato.
sides_rules.color_diversity: Aim for greens, oranges, reds, purples across the week's sides.

shopping_split.costco: Bulk proteins, dairy (butter, sour cream, cheese blocks), tortillas, rice, pantry staples with long shelf life. Prefer Costco for anything that freezes or keeps.
shopping_split.kroger: Fresh produce (fruits, vegetables, herbs), spices, bread/baguettes, and anything perishable that can't be portioned and frozen.

household_rules.weekly_sweet_policy: Do not include a weekly sweet/treat by default. The family goes off script for sweets, so omit sweet recipes and sweet ingredients from standard meal plans and shopping lists unless Justin explicitly asks.
